title: Finite exceptional sets descend through trait conductor pushouts
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $C,W\to S$ be projective flat finitely presented families with nodal geometric curve fibres [def-kun-projective, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $B,N$ be finite etale $S$-schemes, $B\to N$ finite etale of constant degree two, and let $B\hookrightarrow C$, $B\hookrightarrow W$ be closed immersions into the relative smooth loci [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Empty $B,N$ are allowed. Write $X=C\amalg_BN$ and $Y=W\amalg_BN$ for the scheme pushouts of these diagrams [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; assume both pushout squares are cartesian, their curve-to-pushout maps are finite and surjective and their $N$-maps are closed immersions, and restriction to the inverse images of every open in either pushout is again a pushout. Assume also $X,Y\to S$ are projective, flat and finitely presented with nodal geometric curve fibres. The complements are $C\setminus B\cong X\setminus N$ and $W\setminus B\cong Y\setminus N$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $r:T\to C$ be a finite composition of blowups of reduced closed special-fibre points, with $T$ regular, a finite disjoint union of integral surfaces of dimension two [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $q:W\to T$ be proper and birational on matched components, with $W$ reduced and $q_K$ an isomorphism [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme]; birational means it matches generic points and induces isomorphisms on their local rings [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Suppose $h=rq$ restricts on the supplied copy of $B$ to $B\hookrightarrow C$. Let $U_q\subseteq T$ be the maximal open over which $q$ is an isomorphism. Then $T\setminus U_q$ is a finite set of closed special-fibre points. Let $D\subset C$ be its image under $r$, together with the images in $C$ of all centres in the sequence defining $r$, and let $Z$ be the image of $D$ under $C\to X$. Both $D$ and $Z$ are finite sets of closed special-fibre points. The induced pushout morphism $p:Y\to X$ restricts to an isomorphism $p^{-1}(X\setminus Z)\cong X\setminus Z$. This includes points on the image of $N$; no exclusion of persistent horizontal nodes is necessary. Here nodal geometric curve fibres are nonempty reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one whose nonsmooth closed points over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ have completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$; they may be disconnected [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

proof.text: The DVR $R$ is Noetherian: each ideal is principal, hence finitely generated [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Thus $S$ is locally Noetherian by its single affine chart [pqf-def-locnoeth], and is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Projectivity of $C/S$ implies properness [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence finite type [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Consequently $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; preliminary Noetherian reduction for varieties.tex Tag 0BFP.

proof.text: Induct along the finite blowup sequence. On a Noetherian scheme the ideal of a reduced closed point is of finite type, since on each affine open every ideal is finitely generated [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The next blowup is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], hence of finite type by [pqf-lem-proper-basic], so its source is again Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The zero-length sequence starts with $C$. Composition of proper maps [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] shows that $r$ and every prefix of the sequence are proper. In particular $T$ is Noetherian.

source.place: lemma-blowing-up-projective; properness and Noetherianity of the finite sequence.

proof.text: Write $E=T\setminus U_q$, a closed subset. At each point of $T$ the local ring is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. In local dimension one it is a DVR by [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]. Apply clauses (1),(2) of [lem-sfb-normal-modification-codimension-one] to $q$: the target is Noetherian by Step 2, $q$ is proper and birational with exactly the generic-point and local-ring meaning required there, and $W$ is reduced. Every point of local dimension zero or one belongs to $U_q$.

By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], any $t\in E$ has a chain of two strict generalizations. If $t$ had a strict specialization $t'$, adjoining $t'$ would give a chain of three strict inclusions of irreducible closed subsets in its component, contradicting the assumed dimension two [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Hence $t$ is closed. Now [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite] makes $E$ finite. Moreover $T_K$ is open (it is the inverse image of $D(\pi)\subset S$ for a uniformizer $\pi$), and $q_K$ is an isomorphism; maximality gives $T_K\subseteq U_q$. Thus every point of $E$ is in the special fibre.

source.place: Tag 02IZ, lemma-codimension-local-ring; Tag 0BA8, lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components; dimension-two consequence of varieties.tex Tag 0BFP.

proof.text: A proper map is closed by the universally closed assertion of [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Therefore $r(E)$ and the image of every closed centre under its prefix map to $C$ consist of closed special-fibre points. There are finitely many of these points, so their union $D$ is finite and closed. Put $a:C\to X$. Since $a$ is finite, it is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Thus $Z=a(D)$ is likewise a finite closed set of special-fibre points.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, finite exceptional set and its proper images; morphisms.tex Tag 01WN, lemma-finite-proper.

proof.text: Set $C^0=C\setminus D$. At each stage the inverse image of $C^0$ misses the centre, since $D$ includes that centre's image in $C$. Applying [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] successively gives $r^{-1}(C^0)\cong C^0$. Also $r^{-1}(C^0)$ misses $E$, since $D$ includes $r(E)$, so it lies in $U_q$. Restricting $q$ there and composing proves $h^{-1}(C^0)\xrightarrow{\sim}C^0$.

source.place: Complement of the centre; finite iteration and restriction of the two isomorphisms.

proof.text: The maps $a h:W\to X$ and $N\to X$ agree on $B$ by the hypothesis on $h|_B$, hence the pushout property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] supplies $p:Y\to X$. Put $X^0=X\setminus Z$, $Y^0=p^{-1}X^0$, $V=a^{-1}X^0$, and $N^0=N\times_X X^0$. Then $V\subseteq C^0$, so Step 6 restricts to $h^{-1}V\xrightarrow{\sim}V$. The inverse-image diagram for $Y^0$ has its $W$-term equal to $h^{-1}V$ and its $N$-term equal to $N^0$, by $p|_W=a h$ and $p|_N=(N\to X)$. Its $B$-term is the same open $B^0$ of the supplied $B$ as in the inverse-image diagram for $X^0$, again by $h|_B=(B\hookrightarrow C)$.

source.place: Tag 0E25, proposition-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral, compatibility with open restriction; here this is an explicit hypothesis.

proof.text: Both restricted squares are pushouts by hypothesis. The isomorphism $h^{-1}V\to V$ is the identity on the supplied $B^0$, in the sense that its composite with $B^0\hookrightarrow h^{-1}V$ is $B^0\hookrightarrow V$. Thus its inverse and the identity on $N^0$ agree on $B^0$ and induce $s:X^0\to Y^0$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Each of $p s$ and $s p$ agrees with the identity after precomposing with both terms of its pushout cocone, so uniqueness in that same universal property makes them identities. This proves $Y^0\cong X^0$. No point of $N^0$ was removed in this argument: the whole $N^0$ term and both of its branches are present. Empty $B,N,E$ and a zero-length blowup sequence obey the same universal-property argument.

source.place: Tag 0E25, open-restriction construction; elementary uniqueness of pushouts for the resulting isomorphic diagrams.
